items.title: Vance’s Gamble Looks Shakier Now
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. Without Donald Trump’s backing, J. D. Vance was a wealthy man and a best-selling author, but he wanted more. With Trump’s backing, Vance wagered, he might become president. For a while, that looked like a good bet: Trump helped Vance overcome an underwhelming campaign to become a senator from Ohio, then chose him as a running mate in 2024. Trump treated him as his heir apparent, and Vance’s most obvious rival, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, said he wouldn’t run in 2028 if the veep did. Vance’s gamble is looking shakier now. In a 60 Minutes interview this weekend, Trump said he might not endorse anyone in the coming GOP primary. “I may or may not get involved,” he said . “I don’t know. Maybe I’m better off not getting involved.” No one, not even Trump, can say whether he’ll really stay out of it, but he famously enjoys pitting his aides and employees against one another , which a withheld endorsement might achieve. Besides, Trump is at a political low after the midterms, and forcing would-be successors to compete for his favor is one way he can still exert control. Then again—Trump is at a political low. Would his endorsement be much of a prize for Vance, or anyone else? This is the bind that any aspiring Republican presidential candidate will confront ahead of 2028: They need Trump’s support, or at least can’t afford his animosity, because even in his weakened state, his base remains loyal and potentially decisive in a primary. But as the GOP’s disastrous results this month show, being seen as too close to Trump can also be a major liability. You can watch Vance attempting to navigate this trap in recent days. In a lengthy postelection analysis on X, the vice president—a reported skeptic of the war in Iran—pinned the blame for poor Republican performance on the war. This had the advantage of distracting from all the other unpopular parts of the MAGA platform that Vance does support, but it also looks a lot like either a criticism of Trump or an attempt to nudge him into an anti-war position—risky either way. Yesterday, Trump announced that he was pulling Vance off his duty of negotiating with Iran, assigning him instead “to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.” (How this is different from Vance’s previous detail as “fraud czar” is not totally clear—though given Democratic gains at the state level this month, the remit has certainly widened.) Trump added that “we don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed.” The new assignment is a Rorschach test. Is it a punishment for Vance for getting out of line on Iran? (The vice president was also reportedly considering new direct talks with Iran when Trump made the change.) Is Trump giving Vance a thankless, amorphous task that will further alienate domestic audiences who have already turned against the White House? Or is Trump helping Vance by pulling him off a dead-end role and allowing him to create some distance from the Iran debacle? (Trump could also just be acting impulsively.) Vice presidents tend to get stuck with these types of vague, impossible tasks, which later become electoral baggage. It was one of Kamala Harris’s big challenges in 2024. But Vance and Harris share a larger disadvantage. “There basically isn’t any good example since presidential approval ratings began of the VP to an unpopular president later being elected president himself,” Nate Silver notes . Maybe that’s one reason, according to a CNN report today , “Vance has given serious consideration to not running for president in 2028 after last week’s calamitous midterm elections.” The article cites conversations with “roughly a dozen allies and advisers.” Yet The Washington Post also reports today that Vance is “still more likely to run for president than not,” a conclusion based on conversations with—you guessed it—“more than a dozen people with a view into the vice president’s orbit.” Although Vance has consistently led 2028-primary polls at this early stage, a Reuters/Ipsos poll this week found Rubio slightly ahead of him . One poll is just one poll, and I’ve written that Rubio will have the same can’t-win-with-Trump, can’t-win-without-him dynamic that Vance does, especially because he’s the secretary of state and national security adviser during the Iran war. (There’s also the matter of him using taxpayer money to fly military jets to watch his son’s football team, as my colleague Sally Jenkins writes today.) But the result does suggest Vance’s vulnerability. With the nomination looking more available, other Republicans are also suddenly making themselves visible. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis offered some sharp statements about the direction of the GOP after the midterms, evidently positioning himself as an alternative. But the 2024 Republican primary showed DeSantis’s limits as a campaigner—and the difficulty he faced in trying to be both an inheritor and alternative to Trumpism. Former Vice President Pence is interested too ; a Pence campaign would test whether a Republican can win with the rare combination of being both tainted by association with Trump and also detested by him. Louisiana Senator John Kennedy apparently wants to see whether a candidate can succeed on the basis of folksy aphorisms delivered in an exaggerated drawl . On Kalshi, the prediction market, traders still see Vance as the most likely nominee , but they have John McEntee as fourth. McEntee is no household name; he was a personal aide to Trump in his first term but was pushed out over alleged problem gambling, and since then has become a TikTok influencer and the founder of a right-wing dating site. Whether McEntee’s place in the market is more an indictment of Kalshi’s usefulness or the 2028 Republican presidential bench is difficult to say. Related: Trump isn’t setting Vance or Rubio up for the future. The shamelessness of Marco Rubio Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : Biden: I was right to seek reelection. The Democrats who are stunned to find themselves in Congress John Ullyot: “I’ve been with Trump since 2016. Hegseth should resign.” Today’s News Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the Commerce Department for failing to blacklist Megaspeed , a Singaporean company under investigation for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned over a series of revelations about extramarital affairs, including one with a woman who led Megaspeed and is linked to Chinese intelligence. Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland announced last night that he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader , calling for new leadership after Democrats’ midterm victories. Van Hollen said that more than 10 senators have pledged their support, while Schumer said he has enough votes to retain the position in a December leadership election. Representative Lauren Boebert, a Republican, narrowly lost her reelection bid in Colorado to the Democrat Eileen Laubacher, a retired Navy rear admiral, according to the Associated Press. Dispatches The Books Briefing : Boris Kachka on the writers who tried to reconstruct the past . Explore all of our newsletters here. Evening Read Illustration by Mojo Wang The People Working to Keep Their AI Partners Alive By Victoria Turk Whenever AI companies release new models, die-hard users tend to greet the updates with a wave of grumbling about changes to how a model responds to prompts, how it integrates into their workflow, or, simply, the way it speaks. Most people soon get used to the latest release, ready to gripe again when the next one comes along. But for one niche group of particularly fervent AI users, model updates represent a much more alarming proposition. These are people who have developed what they consider to be intimate relationships with AI products. For them, AI has become a companion—a kind of friend, partner, or even lover—and any change to the underlying model poses something akin to an existential threat. Read the full article. items.title: Manso Keniago Chief challenges NAIMOS to prove alleged shooting that killed six
items.description: The Chief of Manso Keniago in the Amansie West District has challenged the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) to provide evidence of the alleged attack on its men that warranted a reprisal attack on the community. The clash between operatives of the task force and the community has left six people dead and several others, including a toddler, injured. According to the community, the sporadic shooting by NAIMOS was unprovoked, contrary to claims by the anti-illegal mining task force. The streets of Manso Keniago are engulfed in grief and anger. Residents, many clad in black and red, upon hearing that the death toll had increased to six, mourned while the youth were agitated and openly hostile. According to the community, the military started shooting sporadically after traditional authorities attempted to stop them from tracking an excavator confiscated by NAIMOS on a newly tarred road. The Chief, Nana Obeng Mensah Ababio, explains that some of the deceased were shot in their homes. He explained that some victims were killed while fleeing or even while indoors. “Here are pellets from the rifles they shot. I have handed some to the police. The young lady they killed was in the bathroom when the NAIMOS operatives went in to shoot her. Another victim is a male who operates a food joint. They killed him as he was running from his food joint,” he said. Nana Mensah Ababio further disputed claims that the community mobilized to attack the task force at the site of an excavator, insisting the engagement was only between himself and some chiefs. “They did not go to the excavator. It was only me and the chiefs, and it was filmed. If government wants the truth, they should ask NAIMOS to release the drone footage. They filmed everything,” he added. The community further insists the operatives did not come under attack to warrant the shooting and says pictures of a vehicle riddled with bullets, allegedly shot at by the community, are untrue. It took police intervention to stop angry youth from attacking the District Chief Executive, Benjamin Marfo, who they claim failed to come to their aid during the shooting. Calls for an independent investigation into the matter have heightened. Aside from calling for an investigation, the Manso Adubia NDC is demanding that NAIMOS be withdrawn pending the outcome of the investigation.

items.title: I’ve Been With Trump Since 2016. Hegseth Should Resign.
items.description: “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times.” The loud rebuke of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his entourage by an Army sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day was the latest embarrassment of the defense chief’s tenure. For nearly two years, Hegseth has treated the Pentagon as a backdrop for self-promotion. He would serve President Trump best by stepping down before Democrats use him to help jam up the president’s agenda during Trump’s final two years in office. I do not say that lightly. I first worked for Trump on his 2016 campaign in Trump Tower. I served in his White House as a deputy assistant to the president and chief spokesperson for the National Security Council. In Trump’s second term, I volunteered to help Hegseth stand up his press office by serving him for a short time as a senior adviser and spokesperson. Twenty years ago, I was spokesperson for the Senate Armed Services Committee when another defense secretary became the face of an unpopular war and a millstone around the neck of President George W. Bush. As I write in my new memoir of my years working for Trump, loyalty in his second term has usually been measured by how loudly an appointee defends him. But real loyalty means sometimes telling the president what he does not want to hear, including about yourself. An appointee whose missteps are hurting the president needs to think hard about whether he has become a political liability and offer to step aside when that’s the case. That duty begins before an appointee accepts the job. If the president offered me the post of deputy attorney general, the loyal answer would be, “Thank you, Mr. President. I’m flattered. But you might want someone with a law degree.” Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend co-host and major in the Minnesota National Guard who had never run a large organization, should have known that he was not qualified to lead the largest department in the federal government. He was confirmed 51 to 50 , with the vice president breaking the tie. A nominee who squeaks in on that margin has every reason to lower the volume. He turned it up instead. [ Tom Nichols: Pete Hegseth lashes out ] On January 3, Democrats will take firm control of the House . The 211–204 vote to shelve an impeachment resolution this week, with 11 Democrats not present, was a reprieve for Hegseth, not a vindication. Whether or not Democrats impeach him next year, they will have the gavels and the subpoena power, and every hearing on Hegseth will be a week the White House spends doing something other than advancing its agenda. Hegseth is the least qualified defense secretary in modern memory. Voters have noticed: 32 percent approve and 57 percent disapprove of his performance, according to a Quinnipiac poll from September. He has been the Cabinet’s most visible champion of a war in Iran that has cost more than a dozen American lives, closed the Strait of Hormuz, and burned through nearly 80 percent of our THAAD (Terminal High Altitude Area Defense) interceptors. He has turned the military into a stage in the culture wars. At Marine Corps Base Quantico in September, before an audience the Pentagon had screened based on waist-to-height standards , he said : “No fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors.” He added, “The ideological clowns are out. The patriotic cowboys are in, with testosterone testing on top.” He films workouts with troops and posts them to official accounts . He planned to livestream the firing-squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter until Trump called off the macabre spectacle. [ Read: Democrats are ready to run Hegseth ‘out of town’ ] He has pushed out top military leaders and two of the three service secretaries the president appointed, Dan Driscoll and John Phelan . Two of his closest advisers were marched out of the Pentagon over leak accusations that went nowhere. He undermined the chain of command by intervening in at least two investigations into dangerous low-altitude flights . He shared prestrike details of a U.S. operation in Yemen over Signal with his wife, his brother, and his lawyer, which the Pentagon’s inspector general found had risked “ potential harm to U.S. pilots .” In September 2025, a follow-up, or “double tap,” strike on an alleged drug boat in the Caribbean killed two survivors clinging to the wreckage, after which The Washington Post reported that Hegseth had given a verbal order to “kill everybody.” He denies making the order, but lawmakers in both parties have warned that it could be a war crime . Each of these is a hearing waiting to happen. I have seen how this kind of circus ends. In 2006, Republicans lost both the House and the Senate in a midterm dominated by another unpopular war in the Middle East. Then–Defense Secretary Donald Rumsfeld read the political mood and stepped down rather than weaken his boss and his party by hanging on. Bush replaced him with Robert Gates, whose low-key professionalism steadied the Pentagon. Rumsfeld’s departure was an act of loyalty. Hegseth has chosen the opposite path. This week, at his first press conference in six months, he shouted scripted bromides into the cameras for his customary audience of one, arguing that he should keep his job. When a defense secretary has to make a public case that he is not an embarrassment to the president, he has already lost the battle. Hegseth awarded a medal to the sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier after a public backlash. But it should not take a soldier to remind a secretary of defense about the decorum his office demands. The president deserves better, as do the members of our military.

items.title: FG records 16 Nigerian deaths in Addis Ababa, warns travellers
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has warned Nigerians, particularly those with pre-existing medical conditions, to exercise caution when travelling through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, following the deaths of 16 Nigerians in the city this year. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a travel advisory issued on Friday, stating that the deaths recorded by Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa were reportedly linked to health complications associated with the city’s high altitude. The ministry explained that Addis Ababa is situated approximately 2,355 metres (7,726 feet) above sea level, where lower atmospheric pressure results in reduced oxygen availability. It noted that the conditions could pose increased health risks to travellers with certain underlying medical conditions, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory ailments. According to the advisory, although healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, people with certain pre-existing health conditions may experience complications. The Federal Government therefore advised Nigerians whose medical conditions could be worsened by high altitudes to seek appropriate medical advice before undertaking journeys involving transit through the Ethiopian capital. It also urged travellers with underlying medical conditions to consult medical professionals and obtain necessary guidance before embarking on their trips. The ministry, however, clarified that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa. Rather, it said the notice was aimed at ensuring that medically vulnerable travellers were adequately informed about the possible effects of high altitudes and took necessary precautions. The advisory stated, “This year, Nigeria’s Diplomatic Mission in Addis Ababa has recorded 16 deaths involving Nigerians transiting through the city, reportedly linked to health complications associated with high altitudes. “While healthy individuals are generally able to adapt to reduced oxygen levels in high-altitude environments, persons with certain pre-existing medical ailments, particularly cardiovascular and respiratory conditions, may experience increased health risks in such conditions. “In view of the foregoing, Nigerians with pre-existing health conditions that can be exacerbated by high altitudes are strongly advised to exercise caution when planning journeys that involve transit through Addis Ababa. “Travellers with underlying medical conditions are also urged to obtain appropriate medical guidance before undertaking such journeys.” The ministry reiterated that the advisory was not intended to discourage Nigerians from travelling to or transiting through Addis Ababa but to ensure that those vulnerable to the physiological effects of high altitudes were adequately informed. It reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to protecting the health, safety and wellbeing of Nigerians travelling abroad, adding that it would continue to provide timely information and guidance to safeguard their welfare. items.title: SpaceX to attempt double catch of huge Starship rocket
items.description: SpaceX will attempt to catch both parts of its huge Starship rocket after it launches on its next test flight on Friday. Elon Musk’s company will use the mechanical arms – nicknamed chopsticks – on its launch tower to grab the rocket parts mid-air as they return to Earth. If successful, this will be the first full recovery of a rocket that’s been to space, paving the way for making Starship reusable so it can fly repeatedly. Nasa will be closely watching the flight: the SpaceX rocket is set to play a vital part in its Artemis programme, which will see astronauts land on the Moon. The lower section of Starship has been recovered three times by the “chopsticks” on the launch tower The 124m-tall rocket is scheduled to blast off from the Starbase launchpad in Texas at 1645 local time (2245 GMT) with a 75-minute-long launch window. After six and a half minutes, the first planned catch will be attempted when the bottom part of the rocket – the Super Heavy booster – returns to the launch tower. The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, will continue its journey to space and deploy 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high speed internet from space. The Ship is then due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning for the second catch attempt about 22 and a half hours after taking off. Until now, SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead it’s splashed down in the ocean. SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it’s in space. If any problems are detected there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. A SpaceX lander could take astronauts down to the surface of the Moon Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX. In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster. Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than a hundred times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch. But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, President of Royal Aeronautical Society. “A successful double catch would be visually spectacular, but full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space,” he said. “One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate.” After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency. The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa’s attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 – a highly ambitious timeline. SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface. But it’s not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down. Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule. This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa’s Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin’s landers. Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments – the pace of the rocket’s development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended. But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida. Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027. Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

items.title: Kidnappers kill Kaduna farmer after collecting N56m ransom
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Armed kidnappers have reportedly killed an Abuja-based worker and farmer, Ibrahim Kadafa, popularly known as Ibro, after collecting N56 million ransom and other valuables from his family following his abduction along the Kaduna-Abuja highway. Kadafa was abducted alongside his friend, Mustapha Shelpidi, on October 28, 2026, while supervising the harvesting of soybeans on his farm around Alheri Camp, Kilometre 30, along the Kaduna-Abuja road. The two friends were reportedly seized when armed men invaded the farm and took them to an undisclosed location. Following the abduction, the kidnappers initially demanded N100 million ransom from the family but later reduced the amount to N80 million after negotiations. A family source said that in a desperate effort to secure Kadafa’s release, the family eventually raised and paid N56 million, alongside three brand-new Samsung mobile phones and a recharge card worth N20,000. The payment was reportedly made within two weeks of negotiations, as the family struggled to meet the demands of the abductors in the hope of securing his safe return. However, the family’s hope of reuniting with him was shattered on Wednesday, November 11, when they reportedly received his lifeless body instead. The source disclosed that Kadafa sustained a gunshot injury to his leg while allegedly attempting to escape during the abduction but was reportedly denied access to medical attention throughout his captivity. The family reportedly suspects that complications arising from the untreated gunshot wound may have contributed to his death, although the exact circumstances surrounding his demise remain unclear. The incident has renewed concerns over the activities of armed kidnappers along the Kaduna-Abuja highway, where travellers and residents of adjoining farming communities continue to face security threats. The post Kidnappers kill Kaduna farmer after collecting N56m ransom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death
items.description: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was suspended for 12 matches by the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee on Friday after his challenge on Jesus de Miguel resulted in the death of the Tenerife striker last week. Equatorial Guinea international Owono was sent off in the second division clash on November 2 after racing into midfield and colliding with De Miguel while trying to clear an aerial ball. After the collision De Miguel, 30, was placed in intensive care in hospital and the Spanish forward died on November 3. “The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’,” said the committee in a statement. “The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. “In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.” Spanish police sources last week told AFP an investigation into what happened had been opened under judicial supervision. Owono said he was enduring the “hardest days of my life” after De Miguel’s death. “These are the hardest days of my life. I struggle to find the words and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened,” said Owono in a statement published by his club Andorra last week. “I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. “I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesus.” FC Andorra coach Carles Manso said Thursday it would be Owono who decides if and when he returns to football after the tragic incident. On Saturday Tenerife fans and players gathered at the club’s stadium for a memorial and farewell to De Miguel. His funeral took place last Thursday and around 400 mourners attended, including Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Real Madrid president Florentino Perez. The post Goalkeeper Owono suspended for 12 matches after De Miguel death appeared first on Vanguard News .

Siguiri : Alpha Condé dénonce une « répression d’une brutalité inacceptable » et réclame une enquête indépendante
items.description: L'ancien président guinéen a adressé un message de solidarité aux populations de Siguiri, après les violences liées à l'orpaillage artisanal. Il met en cause l'entourage du général Mamadi Doumbouya. L'ancien chef de l'État guinéen Alpha Condé a adressé un message de « solidarité et de compassion » aux populations de Siguiri, dans le nord-est de la Guinée, à la suite des « événements tragiques » survenus dans cette région aurifère. Il y exprime sa « profonde consternation » et une « indignation difficilement contenue » face à ce qu'il qualifie de « répression d'une brutalité inacceptable » contre des populations qui, selon lui, « ne réclament que le droit de vivre dignement sur leur propre terre ». Le président déchu en septembre 2021 dit son soutien aux familles endeuillées, aux blessés et à ceux dont les activités économiques ont été « brutalement interrompues ». Il estime que leur détresse « ne saurait être ignorée, encore moins criminalisée ». L'orpaillage, « une pratique ancestrale » Alpha Condé défend l'orpaillage artisanal, qu'il décrit comme une activité « enracinée depuis des siècles » dans les traditions de Siguiri. Des générations entières en ont vécu, rappelle-t-il, et il juge « historiquement injuste » de présenter les populations locales comme « des intruses » sur leurs propres terres. Il s'interroge : comment une activité qui a longtemps coexisté avec l'exploitation industrielle est-elle devenue « subitement un problème d'ordre public » ? Il pointe plutôt l'expansion « incontrôlée » de l'exploitation mécanisée ces dernières années à Siguiri et Mandiana, qui s'est faite selon lui sans encadrement environnemental rigoureux ni contrôle administratif transparent. Des accusations visant l'entourage de Mamadi Doumbouya L'ancien président évoque des « accusations graves » sur l'implication de l'entourage et de la famille du général Mamadi Doumbouya dans le parrainage d'intérêts privés étrangers actifs dans le secteur. Il demande une enquête indépendante pour établir « qui a autorisé, protégé ou facilité ces activités » et au bénéfice de qui. Il demande aussi que les violences signalées contre des civils (morts, blessés, destructions de biens) soient condamnées et fassent l'objet d'enquêtes indépendantes. « Les populations civiles ne sont pas les ennemies de la République. Elles en sont la raison d'être », écrit-il. Un appel à la fraternité ouest-africaine Alpha Condé juge « particulièrement révoltant » que les orpailleurs venus des pays voisins soient désignés comme « boucs émissaires ». Il rappelle que des Guinéens pratiquent eux aussi l'orpaillage au Mali, au Burkina Faso et au Ghana. Pour lui, la fraternité africaine ne peut pas être une valeur « revendiquée selon nos intérêts ». Il s'en prend aussi au discours souverainiste des autorités de transition. Le soutien accordé aux dirigeants issus du coup d'État du 5 septembre 2021 « ne constituait nullement un chèque en blanc », affirme-t-il, ni une autorisation de disposer des ressources nationales au profit d'intérêts particuliers. « On ne peut dénoncer l'impérialisme dans les discours tout en laissant prospérer des mécanismes de captation des richesses africaines », ajoute-t-il. L'État a le devoir de réglementer le secteur minier, reconnaît l'ancien président, mais « réglementer ne signifie pas exclure » et « faire respecter la loi ne signifie pas autoriser la violence ». Il conclut en souhaitant que l'or de Siguiri devienne « une richesse partagée » et non « une malédiction » pour ceux qui vivent sur cette terre.

Photos from ‘Democracy Is Not for Sale’ dialogue in Oti Region
items.description: JoyNews’ Democracy Is Not for Sale dialogue took place in Dambai in the Oti Region, bringing together stakeholders and members of the public to examine the growing influence of money in Ghana’s electoral process. The engagement, held at the Dambai College of Education on Friday, November 13, focused on vote buying, political financing and the implications of financial inducements for the country’s democratic development. The dialogue provided a platform for participants to reflect on how money influences voting decisions, the factors that make voters vulnerable to inducements and the need to protect the integrity of elections. A key concern surrounding vote buying is its potential to undermine the freedom of voters to make independent choices and weaken public confidence in the electoral process. The engagement forms part of JoyNews’ broader effort to promote public awareness and encourage national conversations on electoral accountability, transparency in political financing and the responsibilities of citizens in safeguarding Ghana’s democracy. Adomonline’s photojournalist, Joseph Odotei, was on the ground and took these photos.

items.title: Lagos NDC meeting attack threatens democracy — APM candidate
items.description: By Dapo Akinrefon The governorship candidate of the Action Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Laja Adeoye, has condemned the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during their town hall meeting in Lagos, describing the incident as shameful and a threat to democracy. Adeoye said the disruption of the meeting at Classique Event Centre, Oregun, Ikeja, on Thursday, amounted to an infringement on the constitutional rights of citizens to assemble and freely express their political views. He warned that the use of thugs to disrupt opposition gatherings could heighten political tension ahead of the 2027 general elections. Adeoye said, “Nobody should be attacked for supporting a candidate of his or her choice. What happened in Lagos on Thursday was shameful and unacceptable in a democracy.” He described the incident as particularly disturbing, noting that Lagos had traditionally been regarded as a centre of political activities where parties and candidates could canvass for support. According to him, the attack was not merely against the NDC but also against the democratic process and Nigerians who believe in free and fair elections. The APM candidate urged the Lagos State Police Command to identify, arrest and prosecute those responsible for the incident, irrespective of their political affiliation or status. He warned that failure to bring the perpetrators to justice could encourage similar attacks in other parts of the country as political activities gather momentum ahead of the 2027 elections. Adeoye also expressed concern over the safety of voters, candidates and journalists during the campaign period, recalling reports that a journalist covering the meeting was attacked and dispossessed of his working equipment. He called on political leaders to rise above partisan interests and condemn violence, stressing that democracy could not thrive in an atmosphere of fear and intimidation. The APM candidate commended the NDC supporters for maintaining their composure despite the alleged provocation, saying their conduct demonstrated commitment to democratic values. “The supporters did not retaliate. They conducted themselves in a peaceful manner. That is the spirit we need to sustain our democracy,” he said. He urged political parties to caution their supporters against violence and embrace issue-based campaigns rather than intimidation and thuggery. Adeoye also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), security agencies and other political stakeholders to work together to guarantee a level playing field for all parties ahead of the 2027 elections. He said Lagos, as the country’s commercial nerve centre, should demonstrate that elections could be contested and won without violence. He further urged the National Peace Committee and civil society organisations to intervene by encouraging political actors to embrace peaceful political engagement. According to him, Nigerians were more concerned about finding solutions to insecurity, unemployment, rising cost of living and poor infrastructure than political violence. Adeoye sympathised with those reportedly injured during the attack and wished them a speedy recovery, while urging the NDC to remain focused on its campaign. “We must not allow a few disgruntled elements to derail our democracy. The 2027 election must be about ideas, not violence,” he said. He reaffirmed the APM’s commitment to peaceful, credible and transparent elections, as well as respect for the rule of law and democratic values. items.title: Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order
items.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia A group of 601 retired civil servants in Nasarawa State has commenced enforcement of a court order directing the recovery of over ₦4 billion in outstanding gratuities and other entitlements owed them by the state government. The pensioners, under the aegis of the Concerned Group of Nasarawa State Pensioners, secured a consent judgment against the state government in 2020 over the alleged non-payment of their retirement benefits. Their spokespersons, Mr Simon Auna and Mallam Usman Adamu, disclosed the development while speaking with journalists in Lafia on Friday. The group said it subsequently obtained an order from the National Industrial Court, Makurdi, awarding 25 per cent post-judgment interest on the judgment sum, bringing the total amount being sought to over ₦4 billion. According to the pensioners, following the alleged failure of the state government to comply with the judgment, their lawyers approached the Senior District Court in Makurdi, presided over by Justice Ada Jack. The court subsequently directed six commercial banks to release funds belonging to the Nasarawa State Government, amounting to over ₦4 billion, for payment to the affected retirees. In a move to enforce the order, the pensioners’ legal team, accompanied by court bailiffs, visited some branches of one of the commercial banks in Makurdi, Benue State, where they removed some movable properties. Speaking on the development, counsel to the pensioners, Mrs Doofan Sefa-Aii, said the legal team would continue to operate within the law to ensure full recovery of the funds owed the retirees. Another counsel, Mr Awo Matthew, appealed to the Nasarawa State Government and the banks involved to allow the legal process to take its course, considering the hardship the pensioners had endured while pursuing payment of their entitlements. However, the Director of Corporate Services and Arbitration at the Nasarawa State Ministry of Justice, Mr Usman Aliyu, said the state government had taken all necessary legal steps, including filing a motion for a stay of execution of the court order. Meanwhile, Adamu, who is the group’s Lafia Local Government Chairman, and Auna, its Legal Adviser, described the court order as a significant breakthrough after years of seeking payment of their entitlements. They said the development had renewed their hope of recovering the outstanding benefits. The pensioners reaffirmed their determination to pursue their entitlements through lawful means until the matter was resolved. The post Nasarawa pensioners begin enforcement of ₦4bn court order appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment
items.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Professor Babagana Umara Zulum, has announced a ₦50,000 welfare support for each soldier preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe communities in the state, alongside a pledge to provide operational logistics to strengthen security. Zulum gave the assurance on Friday during a visit to the headquarters of the 24 Task Force Brigade in Dikwa Local Government Area, where he met with the Brigade Commander, Brigadier General Aminu Gumel. The governor said the visit was aimed at exploring measures to improve security along the Maiduguri–Mafa–Dikwa–Ngala highway, a strategic economic corridor linking several communities in eastern Borno State. He noted that the highway was vital to trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities, stressing that improved security would enable residents to travel safely, move agricultural produce and rebuild their livelihoods. “My visit is primarily aimed at exploring measures to strengthen security along the strategic economic corridor, which connects Maiduguri to several communities in eastern Borno and serves as a vital route for trade, transportation and cross-border commercial activities,” Zulum said. Addressing troops preparing for deployment to Maiwa and Koshebe, the governor pledged to provide operational logistics and sustained welfare support. He also announced a payment of ₦50,000 to each soldier preparing for the deployment to the two communities. Koshebe has previously suffered deadly attacks by suspected Boko Haram insurgents. On November 28, 2020, insurgents attacked rice farmers working in fields around the community, killing more than 100 people, many of whom were seasonal farm labourers from Sokoto State. Similarly, in November 2023, suspected insurgents attacked farmers harvesting rice in the Karkut and Koshebe areas of Mafa Local Government Area, killing at least 13 people, while others were reported missing. Zulum’s administration has continued to provide logistics and welfare assistance to security agencies as part of efforts to support military operations, improve security and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their communities. The governor was accompanied on the visit by the member representing Monguno/Nganzai/Marte Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Engr. Bukar Talba; member representing Dikwa Constituency in the Borno State House of Assembly, Mohammed Zakariya; Commissioner for Information and Internal Security, Professor Usman Tar; Commissioner for Local Government and Emirate Affairs, Sugun Mai Mele; and other senior government officials. The post Zulum offers soldiers N50,000 each, logistics for Borno deployment appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Politics is an investment, not vote-buying – Oti Regional Minister
items.description: The Oti Regional Minister, John Kwadwo Gyapong, has described electoral politics as an investment, saying that candidates spend money to mobilise support and participate in elections. He said the financial commitments involved in campaigning, including transporting voters and providing for their basic needs during election periods, should be considered part of the investment required to compete for political office. Speaking at JoyNews’ Democracy Is Not for Sale dialogue at the Dambai College of Education on Friday, November 13, he questioned why political spending was often criticised when financial transactions were accepted in other aspects of life. “Who goes to school without paying for it? Who is a storekeeper who goes to buy things without paying? So why is it that when it is time for us to cast our votes during elections, it should be free?” he asked. Mr Gyapong argued that candidates invest resources in their political ambitions because they expect to gain something from the process. “As I stand here, I am a minister. If I don’t do politics, will I become a minister? Do they just pick ministers? As the chief executive is sitting here, did he just get up to become a chief executive? If he doesn’t pay, will he become a chief executive?” he asked. He recalled that when political activities began in 1992, party organisers were already looking for people with the financial capacity to contest elections and engage voters. According to him, candidates were expected to have the means to support their campaigns, including providing basic necessities such as water for people they engaged. Mr Gyapong also cited the cost of transporting voters from long distances to participate in elections, as well as arrangements for their accommodation and food. He said such expenses were part of the resources candidates commit to securing electoral support. “Politics is a game. Everybody who is coming there to vote, they hire a car from Krachi West to cross the river to head to Jasikan to vote for someone who will later get a position and eventually get money to take care of his wife and children,” he said. “If that person is going to vote, you, who want them to vote for you, would make sure you pay for the car they board. You will make sure to check where they will sleep and the food they will eat. So, is that one called sales? It is not sales.” He maintained that the financial commitments involved in elections should be understood as political investment rather than the sale or purchase of votes. “I call it democracy as an investment project because everyone wants to get something out of it. And so, if you want something out of it, then it means you have to invest. And if you have to invest, you don’t call it selling or buying votes; no, it is an investment,” he added.

items.title: COVID-19 loans must be repaid, NIRSAL MFB insists
items.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief NIRSAL Microfinance Bank (NMFB) has clarified that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility (TCF) was an intervention loan, not a grant, stressing that beneficiaries are obligated to repay the funds. The bank said deductions from the accounts of beneficiaries who accessed the facility would continue until their outstanding loans were fully liquidated, in line with the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism. In a statement issued in Abuja at the weekend, the bank explained that the GSI framework allows financial institutions to recover outstanding loan obligations from eligible accounts linked to borrowers’ Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), subject to applicable regulatory guidelines. The bank said the clarification became necessary to address concerns surrounding loan recoveries and reassure customers and members of the public of its commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible banking practices. It explained that the COVID-19 Targeted Credit Facility was introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to support households and businesses affected by the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the bank, all beneficiaries were required to accept electronic offer letters before disbursement, with the documents clearly outlining the terms and conditions of the facility, including repayment obligations and recovery mechanisms in cases of default. “Regarding the recovery process, the Bank operates within the applicable regulatory framework, including the Global Standing Instruction (GSI) mechanism approved by the Central Bank of Nigeria,” it stated. NIRSAL MFB, however, acknowledged concerns raised by some beneficiaries over the timing and amounts of deductions, outstanding loan balances and access to repayment information. The bank said it took the complaints seriously, noting that customers must have access to accurate information about their loan accounts. It stressed that the deductions were intended to settle outstanding contractual obligations, adding that beneficiaries who disputed deductions or identified discrepancies in their repayment records should contact the bank for individual account reconciliation. “Where any beneficiary has concerns about deductions made, discrepancies in repayment records or the status of an outstanding balance, such cases should be brought to the bank’s attention for individual account reconciliation and appropriate resolution,” it said. The bank assured that legitimate complaints would be investigated and that any discrepancies established during the reconciliation process would receive the necessary attention. It urged beneficiaries seeking clarification on their loan status, repayment history or outstanding obligations to contact the bank through its officially designated customer service channels. items.title: Gov’t should fund political parties to end ‘democracy for sale’ – Oti Regional Minister
items.description: The Oti Regional Minister, John Kwadwo Gyapong, has called on the government to provide financial support to political parties, saying that public funding would help address concerns about money influencing electoral competition. He said if Ghanaians wanted to end what is described as the sale of democracy, the state should take responsibility for funding political parties to support their activities. Speaking at JoyNews’ Democracy Is Not for Sale dialogue at the Dambai College of Education on Friday, November 13, Mr Gyapong said that the financial demands of political campaigns make investment an unavoidable part of electoral politics. He said candidates and political parties require resources to mobilise voters, organise campaigns and meet other election-related expenses. The Regional Minister questioned why political spending during elections was treated differently from financial transactions in other aspects of life, including education and healthcare. He argued that candidates invest in politics because they expect to gain political positions and other benefits from the process. Mr Gyapong said he believed the debate about money in elections should therefore move beyond criticising political spending and consider how parties could be adequately funded. “So what I’m saying is that if Ghanaians don’t want to say there is democracy for sale, then the government should take care of the party. “The government should give out money that they will use for the party. Fund political parties. When you fund them, then we are not talking about the sale of democracy,” he said. He maintained that public funding of political parties would provide an alternative source of financial support for their activities and help address the concerns surrounding money in elections.

items.title: Customs intercepts live sea turtle at Nigeria-Benin border
items.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Seme Area Command, has intercepted a live endangered sea turtle allegedly being smuggled through a footpath linking Nigeria and the Republic of Benin. The Olive Ridley Sea Turtle, scientifically known as Lepidochelys olivacea, was intercepted during a routine patrol by Customs officers at about 10.30pm on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The command said the officers sighted a suspicious individual carrying a sack along the border route, but the suspect abandoned the bag and fled into a nearby bush upon noticing the patrol team. According to a statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Customs, John Tunde Ayagbalo, examination of the abandoned sack revealed the live sea turtle concealed inside. He said the animal was immediately secured and kept in safe custody before being handed over to relevant wildlife authorities for proper care, rehabilitation and eventual release into its natural habitat. The Acting Customs Area Controller, Seme Area Command, Deputy Comptroller Norman Olisah Alumanah, described the interception as a demonstration of the vigilance and professionalism of officers in tackling wildlife trafficking. Alumanah warned smugglers, poachers and their collaborators against using the nation’s borders as corridors for illegal wildlife trade, adding that the command had intensified patrols, surveillance and intelligence gathering across its area of responsibility. He also called on residents of border communities to provide credible intelligence to support the fight against wildlife trafficking. The Customs boss said the command would complement enforcement operations with stakeholder education and sensitisation on endangered species, their ecological importance and the legal implications of their unauthorised trade. Wildlife trafficking remains a major environmental crime, threatening biodiversity and the survival of endangered species through illegal exploitation for meat, eggs, shells, traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade. Nigeria is a signatory to the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which regulates international trade in endangered wildlife and plant species. The convention is domesticated in Nigeria through the Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) Act, Cap E9, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. items.title: Ebola: All 62 contacts test negative after monitoring – NCDC
items.description: By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has completed the 21-day monitoring of all 62 contacts linked to the imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease (BVD), a form of Ebola disease, confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, with no secondary infections recorded. The Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, disclosed this on Friday during a media briefing in Abuja, saying the last contact had been discharged from monitoring after testing negative for the virus. Idris said 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period, but laboratory tests confirmed that none had contracted the disease. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case. “A total of 62 contacts were identified, placed in quarantine and followed up by our public health teams. During the monitoring period, 13 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease, and all tested negative,” he said. The index case was a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman, who tested positive for the virus in Abuja on October 20. She was subsequently medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26. Providing an update on her condition, Idris said the woman had recovered and been discharged from a hospital in Geneva. He also disclosed that seven additional suspected cases were reported and investigated in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the past three weeks. All seven cases tested negative for the virus. However, the NCDC chief cautioned against interpreting the completion of contact monitoring as a formal declaration that the outbreak was over. He explained that such a declaration would depend on established public health criteria and findings from continued surveillance. “It is important to note that the completion of contact monitoring does not, by itself, constitute a formal declaration that an outbreak is over. Such a determination must be based on the applicable public health criteria and the findings of ongoing surveillance. “Nigeria therefore remains vigilant, particularly given the continued occurrence of Ebola virus disease in the DRC,” he said. Idris assured Nigerians that disease surveillance and preparedness activities would continue, stressing that the agency remained committed to protecting residents and visitors. Looking ahead to the December festive season, he warned that increased travel, social interactions and large public gatherings could heighten the risk of disease transmission. He identified family celebrations, religious activities, political campaigns, concerts, festivals and sporting events as occasions likely to increase human movement and interaction. He urged anyone who develops symptoms to seek medical attention promptly, warning against automatically assuming that every fever is malaria, particularly among people with recent travel history or possible exposure to infectious diseases. The NCDC boss also advised the public to avoid unprotected contact with the blood and other body fluids of anyone suspected of having Ebola or another infectious disease. He urged individuals identified as contacts to cooperate with public health authorities and comply with monitoring instructions. Idris further called on organisers of mass gatherings, including religious activities, political rallies, concerts, festivals and sporting events, to provide adequate sanitation, safe drinking water, medical assistance and mechanisms for promptly reporting suspected illnesses. Healthcare workers in public and private facilities were also urged to maintain a high index of suspicion, strictly observe infection prevention and control measures, and report suspected cases without delay. On international travel, Idris reminded inbound travellers of the requirement to complete the Nigeria Health Declaration Form before arrival. He encouraged travellers to consult the NCDC website for relevant information, provide accurate details of their health and travel history, and promptly report any symptoms or possible exposure to Port Health authorities. While assuring the public that there was no reason to panic, he said continued vigilance, early reporting and cooperation with health authorities remained essential to preventing the spread of infectious diseases. items.title: 2027: Tinubu, Atiku, Obi not there for Nigeria — Sule Lamido
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Jigawa State Governor and PDP chieftain, Sule Lamido, has dismissed President Bola Tinubu, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, as unsuitable options for Nigeria ahead of the 2027 general election. Lamido stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, where he was asked which of the three political figures could attract the Northern vote in the forthcoming presidential election. Giving his assessment, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) chieftain said none of the three contenders was in a position to address Nigeria’s challenges. He said, “Look, from my own personal opinion, in my view, voting should depend on who is the person with the right kind of quality and calibre to be able to address the same problem. Peter Obi, Tinubu, Atiku — none of them is there for Nigeria.” The former Jigawa governor also declared his support for the PDP’s presidential candidate, Professor Sandy Onor, insisting that he remained committed to the opposition party and would not vote for Tinubu in 2027. Asked whether he had endorsed Tinubu for a second term, Lamido said he remained a PDP member and would vote for his party’s candidate. He said, “I am PDP through and through. I am voting for my candidate, Professor Sandy Onor; that is my candidate. What I’m saying is that we have somebody called Professor Onor on that ballot. I’m voting him.” Lamido’s remarks come amid controversy over claims that he had endorsed Tinubu’s re-election bid after Vice-President Kashim Shettima reportedly listed him among former Jigawa governors backing the President ahead of 2027. However, the Jigawa State chapter of the PDP had earlier dismissed the claim, insisting that Lamido had neither endorsed Tinubu nor defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC. Nwofor, SAN, Ibezim said he was discontinuing the suit to create room for an amicable resolution and settlement of the dispute between the parties. The suit was instituted against Ndukuba, the Archbishop, Metropolitan and Primate of All Nigeria, and Enyindah, the Dean of the Church of Nigeria and chairman of the visitation team to the Diocese of Awka. Ibezim had challenged the constitution of the visitation team, alleging that it was improperly constituted by the first defendant in a letter dated June 17, 2026. However, the notice of withdrawal did not indicate whether the parties had reached any agreement or concluded a settlement over the dispute. items.title: Recours électoraux : la Cour constitutionnelle notifie les députés concernés
items.description: La Cour constitutionnelle a commencé à notifier les députés dont l’élection est contestée, dans le cadre de l’examen de plus de 170 recours déposés à la suite du scrutin législatif du 23 septembre. La Cour constitutionnelle a entamé l’examen des dossiers de recours relatifs au scrutin du 23 septembre dernier, a appris Hespress de sources informées. Les mêmes sources indiquent que la justice constitutionnelle a commencé à ouvrir plusieurs dossiers déposés par des mandataires de listes, dont elle vérifie la conformité avec la législation en vigueur. Elles relèvent également que la Cour a commencé à notifier plusieurs parlementaires élus dont le siège est contesté par des mandataires de listes concurrentes dans leurs circonscriptions. Les sources précitées soulignent que l’instance judiciaire notifie les parties concernées par les recours afin qu’elles préparent leur défense et répondent à leur contenu. Elle se prononcera ensuite sur le sérieux de chaque recours et sur la réponse du député visé, après examen des pièces versées au dossier. Elle pourra aussi demander des éclaircissements aux préfectures et provinces concernées. Selon les mêmes sources, la notification des parties se poursuivra dans les semaines à venir. Cette étape sera accélérée afin de hâter le jugement des recours déposés dans les délais légaux. Des sources de Hespress avaient indiqué précédemment que le nombre de recours introduits devant la Cour constitutionnelle, à Rabat, dépassait 170, tous enregistrés au greffe. Ces sources ont ajouté que de nombreux mandataires de listes ont vu leurs mandants affluer à la Cour, où ils ont déposé leurs requêtes dans les délais légaux, avant la clôture des dépôts. Des dizaines de pièces ont été produites par les mandataires. Elles portent, selon eux, sur des irrégularités qui ont entaché le processus électoral et appellent à en tirer les conséquences juridiques. Les dossiers déposés auprès de la Cour comprennent des procès-verbaux de constat, des extraits de données de téléphones et des attestations. S’y ajoutent des clés USB contenant des vidéos et des photos censées documenter, selon leurs auteurs, des violations du processus électoral. Des vidéos ont également été fournies. Elles documenteraient, selon les auteurs des recours, l’utilisation par des candidats de certaines formations politiques, notamment des présidents de communes ou des élus soutenant les mandataires, de moyens des collectivités territoriales (véhicules de transport, camions, agents occasionnels) au service de leurs intérêts électoraux durant cette période. L’article 32 de la loi organique n° 066.13 relative à la Cour constitutionnelle dispose que l’élection d’un membre du Parlement peut être contestée dans un délai de trente jours suivant la date de proclamation du résultat du scrutin. Les candidats et les parties concernées doivent respecter ce délai pour saisir la Cour de leurs recours. Aux termes de l’article 33 de la même loi organique, la Cour constitutionnelle statue sur les recours relatifs à l’élection des membres du Parlement dans un délai d’un an, à compter de la date d’expiration du délai de recours. Elle peut toutefois dépasser ce délai par décision motivée, lorsque le nombre ou la nature des recours l’exige. The post Recours électoraux : la Cour constitutionnelle notifie les députés concernés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Israel Bans Travel for Prominent Palestinian Rights Defender
items.description: Click to expand Image Shawan Jabarin, head of the al-Haq human rights group, at the organization's offices in the West Bank city of Ramallah, October 23, 2021. © 2021 Majdi Mohammed/AP Photo (Beirut) – Israeli authorities on November 13, 2026, imposed an international travel ban on Shawan Jabarin, the head of Al-Haq, a leading Palestinian human rights organization in the occupied West Bank. The travel ban comes in the context of increasing attacks against Palestinians and civil society groups in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. Al-Haq, along with the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights and Al-Mezan Center for Human Rights, are continuing their critical human rights work despite US sanctions for engaging with the International Criminal Court. Human Rights Watch, with three other human rights organizations, filed a lawsuit in US federal court on August 11 seeking to have the sanctions struck down. The following quote can be attributed to Balkees Jarrah, Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch: “Israeli authorities’ travel ban against Shawan Jabarin, among the most prominent human rights defenders in Palestine, reflects a vindictive effort to punish those advocating for victims of serious crimes. The ban is the latest escalation of Israel’s campaign to silence Palestinian rights groups that document violations of international law and seek accountability. Governments should act to support and protect Palestinian civil society and ensure that they’re able to continue their invaluable work.”

items.title: Democracy Is Not For Sale: Dambai residents demand greater accountability, sensitisation to tackle vote-buying
items.description: Participants at a public forum in Dambai in the Oti Region have called for increased public education on vote-buying and urged politicians to end the monetisation of votes during elections. They also want political parties and elected officials to fulfil promises made to the people of the Oti Region, stressing the need for greater accountability and commitment to development. The call was made during JoyNews’ Democracy Is Not For Sale programme held at the Dambai College of Education, where students, residents and other stakeholders discussed the effects of vote buying on Ghana’s democratic process. Contributors at the forum said more public education was needed to help voters understand the long-term consequences of exchanging their votes for money and other material benefits. They argued that the practice undermines the integrity of elections and shifts attention from issues such as development, good governance and the ability of political candidates to serve their communities. Some participants urged political parties and aspirants to stop using money and other incentives to influence voters, insisting that electoral support should be based on policies, competence and the commitment of candidates to national and local development. The audience also called on politicians to honour promises made during election campaigns, particularly commitments to address the development needs of communities in the Oti Region. They stressed that residents should not be left with unfulfilled promises after elections, urging elected representatives to remain accessible and accountable to the people they serve. Persons with disabilities who participated in the programme also called for greater inclusion in the distribution of national resources and development opportunities. They emphasised the need for their concerns to be recognised in government policies and development programmes to ensure that they benefit from the country’s resources and are not left behind. The discussions also highlighted the responsibility of citizens in protecting the democratic process, with participants encouraged to reject financial inducements and demand transparency from political leaders. The forum forms part of broader efforts to promote electoral integrity and encourage citizens to recognise their role in strengthening Ghana’s democracy.

Lancement du projet Baluo Banko pour la promotion de la culture du manioc
items.description: Les conseils départementaux de Saône-et-Loire et de Sédhiou, en collaboration avec les chambres consulaires des départements précités, ont procédé au lancement du projet « Baluo Banko – Terre nourricière ». Cette initiative vise à promouvoir la culture et la transformation de plusieurs spéculations, dont le manioc. SEDHIOU- La région de Sédhiou est dotée d'un important potentiel agricole et agroalimentaire. Ces avantages constituent un levier majeur pour l'essor de l'économie locale, la création d’emplois et le renforcement de la sécurité alimentaire des populations. C'est dans ce sillage que les conseils départementaux de Saône-et-Loire (France) et de Sédhiou, ainsi que les chambres de commerce de Sédhiou et de Saône-et-Loire, ambitionnent de structurer et de valoriser les ressources agricoles et alimentaires du territoire en vue de contribuer à une souveraineté alimentaire territoriale durable. Cette initiative, qui s’inscrit autour du projet « Baluo Banko – Terre nourricière est née au cours des rencontres de la Conférence permanente des chambres consulaires africaines et francophones (CPCCAF) », a assuré Moussa Souané, président de la Chambre de commerce, d'industrie et d'agriculture de Sédhiou. De son côté Ousmane Diété, 1er vice-président du conseil départemental de Sédhiou, a salué la pertinence du projet Baluo Banko. « Il est d'une importance capitale pour la promotion des produits locaux de Sédhiou, spécifiquement pour la vulgarisation du manioc à travers le département de Sédhiou. Dès lors, un comité de pilotage, chargé d’assurer la gouvernance et la coordination du projet Baluo Banko a été officiellement installé. Par ailleurs, le diagnostic approfondi a permis d’identifier les principales contraintes et potentialités des filières agricoles et alimentaires du territoire, notamment celle du manioc. « C'est dans ce sens que j'invite les bénéficiaires des communes de Djiredji, Oudoucar, Samé Kanté et Marsassoum à s'approprier le projet », a indiqué Ousmane Diété. La formation des jeunes dans la culture et la transformation du Manioc, mais aussi la participation des femmes dans la politique du développement social continent entres autres des activités qui seront développées dans la mise en œuvre de projet Baluo Banko. Jonas Souloubany BASSENE (correspondant)

items.title: Plus de 493 millions de FCFA mobilisés pour soutenir la scolarisation des filles
items.description: Le maintien des filles à l’école passe aussi par la prise en charge des contraintes matérielles et sanitaires qui freinent leur parcours scolaire. Dans cette perspective, le sous-projet « Maintien des filles à l’école » du projet SWEDD+ Sénégal a mobilisé plus de 493 millions de FCFA pour l’acquisition de kits scolaires et d’hygiène menstruelle, mis à la disposition du ministère de l’Éducation nationale en vue de leur distribution aux adolescentes bénéficiaires. Le ministre de l’Éducation nationale, Moustapha Mamba Guirassy, et la ministre de la Famille, de l’Action sociale et des Solidarités, Marie Angélique Mame Selbé Diouf, ont coprésidé, ce vendredi 13 novembre 2026, la cérémonie officielle de réception et de lancement de la distribution de ces équipements. L’initiative bénéficie de l’appui de la Banque mondiale et du Fonds des Nations unies pour la population (FNUAP). D’un montant global de 493 570 647 FCFA, l’opération prévoit la mise à disposition de 18 893 kits scolaires, évalués à 211 692 147 FCFA, ainsi que de 5 925 kits d’hygiène menstruelle, d’une valeur de 281 878 500 FCFA. Les premiers visent à alléger les dépenses des familles et à faciliter l’accès des filles aux fournitures scolaires. Les seconds doivent contribuer à préserver la santé et la dignité des adolescentes, tout en favorisant leur assiduité en classe. Pour le ministre Moustapha Mamba Guirassy, l’accès à l’éducation ne saurait se résumer à une simple inscription dans un établissement scolaire. « Il suppose que chaque enfant puisse apprendre dans des conditions dignes et favorables jusqu'à son terme », a-t-il souligné. L’hygiène menstruelle, un enjeu de maintien à l’école Au-delà de l’appui matériel, cette initiative met en lumière les obstacles qui continuent de compromettre la continuité du parcours scolaire de nombreuses filles. Les difficultés économiques des familles, mais également les contraintes liées à la gestion de l’hygiène menstruelle, peuvent affecter leur présence en classe et leurs conditions d’apprentissage. À travers le sous-projet « Maintien des filles à l’école », intégré au programme SWEDD+, les autorités entendent ainsi agir sur ces facteurs de vulnérabilité. L’objectif est de créer un environnement scolaire plus favorable, dans lequel les adolescentes ne sont pas contraintes de renoncer à leur éducation pour des raisons matérielles ou sanitaires.Cette démarche s’inscrit dans les ambitions de la Vision Sénégal 2050, qui place l’éducation et l’équité au cœur du développement national. A.N

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : Aissatou Mbossé Seck au début et à la fin de l’aventure
items.description: Jeune reporter à Buenos Aires en 2018, elle a vu le drapeau olympique passer au Sénégal. Huit ans plus tard, elle dirige le centre des médias des JOJ Dakar 2026. Rencontre avec Aïssatou Mbossé Seck, qui a vécu l'aventure du début à la fin. Au Centre de conférence Abdou Diouf, à Diamniadio, là où ont travaillé chaque jour les journalistes des JOJ Dakar 2026, Aissatou Mbossé Seck nous reçoit avec le sourire. Elle est ouverte et chaleureuse, et la bonne humeur se lit dans chacun de ses gestes comme dans ses mots. Pour une femme qui gère le centre principal des médias, c'est presque une évidence : veiller à ce que les journalistes travaillent dans de bonnes conditions, c'est aussi savoir les accueillir. Elle est MPC manager, responsable du centre qui leur est dédié. Un poste de l'ombre, au service de ceux qui racontent la compétition. Pour elle, c'est surtout l'aboutissement d'un long chemin. Quand le Sénégal a été désigné pour accueillir les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse, elle y était. « J'y ai assisté en direct, sans que personne ne me raconte l'histoire », dit-elle. Le début, en 2017 Tout commence en 2017, par un appel à candidatures. Le Comité international olympique cherche de jeunes journalistes pour couvrir les Jeux de la Jeunesse : de jeunes reporters pour raconter de jeunes athlètes. Le programme s'appelle Young Reporters. « C'est en 2017 que je suis entrée dans le monde olympique », se souvient-elle. L'année suivante, elle part pour Buenos Aires, où se tiennent les JOJ 2018. Elle y est présente à un moment clé : la passation de drapeau entre l'Argentine et le Sénégal. Autour d'elle, la délégation des athlètes sénégalais, le président Macky Sall et Soham Wardini, alors maire de Dakar. « On nous a remis le drapeau en attendant de nous une belle organisation, et on a relevé le défi », raconte-t-elle. Dans les coulisses, toujours au cœur du projet Les Jeux devaient se tenir en 2022. Ils auront finalement lieu en 2026. Pendant tout ce temps, elle ne quitte pas le projet. Elle a été volontaire pour l'Académie nationale olympique sénégalaise, puis a travaillé pour le CNOSS et enfin pour le comité d'organisation, le COJOJ. « J'ai toujours été au cœur », résume-t-elle. Elle a donc connu le tout début et la toute fin de l'aventure, et l'émotion était au rendez-vous aux deux bouts. « Dès que le Sénégal a été désigné, le travail a commencé avec le comité d'organisation afin d'arriver à la réussite que l'on connaît aujourd'hui. » Réussir, c'était l'unique objectif. « Le seul défi était de réussir, de permettre à la jeunesse de vivre un rêve, de livrer des infrastructures de qualité. » Elle y voyait un autre enjeu : que les Sénégalais fassent leur ce projet, qu'ils se mobilisent pour remplir les sites de compétition et soutenir les athlètes. Elle assure que la peur a existé. « J'avoue que j'ai eu peur à un moment, mais c'était normal d'avoir peur et de stresser puisqu'on voulait tellement bien faire. » Les questions revenaient : les populations allaient-elles répondre en nombre ? La météo serait-elle clémente ? Tout se passerait-il bien ? « Mais les encouragements étaient là, la volonté de bien faire aussi. Les gens nous ont motivés à réussir. » Parmi ceux qui l'ont portée, elle cite d'abord les volontaires. « Ils ont massivement répondu présent et ont fait de cet événement le leur. Même s'ils ne sont pas payés, ils ont été exceptionnels du début à la fin. » Un hommage qu'elle sait, mieux que beaucoup, être mérité : elle a elle-même été volontaire avant de gravir les échelons. Un monde découvert, une mission accomplie Dans la promotion des Jeux, sa priorité était claire : mobiliser les jeunes et leur transmettre les valeurs olympiques. Ces valeurs, elle les a elle-même découvertes en chemin. « Avant, je ne regardais le sport qu'à la télé, et là j'ai participé à l'organisation des Jeux Dakar 2026. C'est un aboutissement, mais c'était aussi une mission. » Ce qui l'a le plus marquée, c'est la découverte. « J'ai découvert beaucoup de sports, j'ai pu découvrir le monde sportif, et j'ai adoré. J'ai beaucoup appris. » Reste la fierté, qu'elle ne cherche pas à cacher. Dakar, Saly et Diamniadio ont accueilli les Jeux « sans problème ». « Tout a été bien fait, dit-elle. C'est un sentiment de fierté immense. » Dans ce centre des médias où les journalistes écrivent l'histoire de ces Jeux, Aissatou Mbossé Seck, toujours souriante, a déjà écrit la sienne. Oumar Boubacar NDONGO-Pape Lamane FAYE-Fatimata Binetou BA
